title: Literacy Learning Modules
before:
Professional Literacy Learning Module Options 

  • AIM Pathways™ is an interactive digital training platform that delivers evidence-based content in the science of reading. Each Steps to Literacy module follows a “learn, practice, apply” cycle and includes teaching techniques, demonstration videos, and printable resources to help educators integrate new strategies into classroom practice. To learn more and access AIM Steps to Literacy Learning Modules, visit here. 
  • Keys to Literacy offers a comprehensive, research-backed approach to sustainable literacy improvement. Their courses integrate evidence-based instruction with systems, structures, and leadership practices that support equitable and effective learning environments. All modules are designed for asynchronous, on-demand access, allowing educators to engage in professional learning on their own schedules. To learn more and register for the Maine Keys to Literacy Courses, visit here. 

Through these master agreements, the Maine DOE is ensuring that Maine educators have affordable opportunities to deepen their expertise and strengthen literacy instruction for all students.

Reimbursement Funding Update

Funding available to reimburse school administrative units for completed AIM Pathways and Keys to Literacy modules has been fully expended. The Maine Department of Education is no longer accepting reimbursement requests for these modules.

School administrative units may continue to access and purchase modules directly from the approved vendors listed above.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Professional Literacy Learning Module Options" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Make a bold line a real heading
decisions.why: "Reimbursement Funding Update" is a paragraph in bold type. It reads as a heading and is spaced like one, but it is not in the page's outline, a screen reader does not announce it, and the contents list cannot link to it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 2 headings are plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 2 addresses are shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — Danielle.M.Saucier@maine.gov → Danielle.m.Saucier@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 2 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 2 job titles sit in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: Through these master agreements, the Maine DOE is ensuring that Maine educators have affordable opportunities to deepen their expertise and strengthen literacy instruction for all students.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 1 description begins with a small letter, because it used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
